title: "Financial Markets and Behaviors — Review"

## Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH)

**Author** : E. Fama, 1960 · Nobel 2013

**Principle** : prices reflect **all** available information → impossible to beat the market consistently.

### The 3 forms

| Form | Information incorporated | Consequence |
|------|--------------------------|-------------|
| **Weak** (*Weak*) | Past prices only | Technical analysis ineffective |
| **Semi-strong** (*Semi-strong*) | All public information | Fundamental analysis ineffective |
| **Strong** (*Strong*) | Public + private information | Even insiders cannot beat the market |

### Critiques of EMH

- Equities persistently overvalued relative to fundamentals
- Soros, Buffett : too consistent to be just lucky
- **Herding behaviour** (*herding behaviour*)
- **Algorithmic trading** (*algorithmic trading*) amplifies inefficiencies
- **Speculative bubbles** (*speculative bubbles*)

::: {.callout-warning title="Traps — Two emblematic examples"}
**Bitcoin bubble (2013)** : price went from ~\$0 to +\$1 000 in one year → pure speculation, incompatible with EMH

**Flash Crash (May 6, 2010)** : Dow Jones −9,2 % (−998 pts) then full recovery in a few minutes, with no fundamental news
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Nobel Paradox 2013"}
Fama (pro-EMH) and Shiller (anti-EMH) shared the same Nobel → **no consensus** on market efficiency.
:::

## Where Do We Exchange?

### Regulated Markets (Exchanges) vs OTC

| Criterion | Regulated market | OTC (*Over The Counter*) |
|-----------|------------------|--------------------------|
| Examples | NYSE, LSE, CME, SIX | Oanda, bond markets |
| Regulation | Strict | Light |
| Clearing | Clearing house ✅ | No clearing ❌ |
| Transparency | High | Low |
| Counterparty risk | Low | Higher |

### Broker vs Market Maker

| Role | *Market Maker* | *Broker* |
|------|---------------|----------|
| Example | Oanda | Dukascopy |
| Inventory | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Risk taken | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Compensation | Bid/ask spread | Commission |

## Financial Assets

| Asset | Key characteristics |
|-------|---------------------|
| **Equity** (*Equity*) | Periodic dividends · residual risk |
| **Bonds** (*Bonds*) | Loan to a state or company · price ∝ 1/rate · coupons + maturity |
| **Commodities** (*Commodities*) | Wheat, oil, gold · traded via **futures** |
| **Currencies** (*Currencies / FX*) | Quoted in **pairs** · interest rate differential · backbone of markets |

::: {.callout-note title="Bonds — Key relation"}
Bond price ↑ when rates ↓ · Bond price ↓ when rates ↑
:::

## Trading Volumes

### World Stock Exchanges (2013)

| Exchange | Volume (Bn USD) |
|----------|-----------------|
| NYSE Euronext US | 6 920 |
| NASDAQ OMX US | 4 748 |
| Tokyo SE | 3 429 |

### Foreign Exchange Market (FX)

- Daily global volume : **~5 000 billion USD/day**
- EUR/USD : **25 %** of volume · USD/JPY : 18 % · GBP/USD : 9 %
- 50 % of transactions = **FX swaps** (*FX swaps*)

EUR/USD flow per second :

$$\frac{5 \times 10^{12} \times 0.25 \times 0.5}{86\,400 \times 2} \approx 3.6 \text{ M USD/s}$$

## Financial Instruments

| Instrument | Definition | Feature |
|------------|-----------|---------|
| **Spot** | Real asset, immediate delivery | Reference base |
| **Forward** | Future agreement at price fixed today · OTC | Counterparty risk |
| **Futures** | Standardised forward · exchange | Clearing house · margin calls |
| **Option** | **Right** (not obligation) to buy (*call*) or sell (*put*) | Premium to pay · leverage |
| **Index** (*Index*) | Basket of assets (S&P 500, CAC 40...) | Diversification |

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Futures Roll Over"}
A futures has an expiration date. Without **roll over** (close + reopen on next contract) →
physical delivery possible (e.g. tons of wheat or barrels of oil !).
:::

## Stylised Facts

**Definition** : robust empirical regularities that distinguish real markets from a simple random walk (*random walk*).

| Stylised fact | Description | Implication |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| **Volatility clustering** (*Volatility clustering*) | Large variations → large variations · small → small | → **GARCH** models |
| **Negative autocorrelation** (*Negative autocorrelation*) | At high frequency, negative lag 1 | Due to *bid-ask bounce* |
| **Scaling laws** (*Scaling laws*) | $\mathbb{E}[\|r\|] \sim \Delta t^{\alpha}$ | Multi-scale self-similarity |
| **Fat tails** (*Fat tails*) | Extreme events far more frequent than normal law | Risk underestimated by Gaussian models |
| **Seasonality** (*Seasonality*) | Daily, weekly, monthly, yearly | Cyclical non-stationarity |
| **Asymmetry** (*Asymmetry*) | Equity markets fall faster than they rise | Negative skewness |
| **Spread / volume correlation** | Spread ↓ when volume ↑ | More liquidity → better prices |
| **Volume / volatility correlation** | Volume ↑ when volatility ↑ | Uncertainty → activity |

::: {.callout-important title="GARCH — The H comes from stylised facts"}
**H** = *Heteroskedasticity* = non-constant variance = volatility clustering. This is precisely what GARCH models.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Fat tails and Gaussian models"}
Using the normal distribution to model returns **strongly underestimates** the probability of extreme events.
Empirical distributions resemble **Lévy** distributions (*Lévy distributions*) more closely.
:::

## Seasonality

### Equities — U-shape profile

- **Peak at open** : reaction to overnight news
- **Mid-day trough** : low activity
- **Peak at close** : closing of daily positions

### Currencies — Global sessions

| Session | GMT Hours | Activity |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Sydney | 22h – 07h | Low |
| Tokyo | 00h – 09h | Moderate |
| London | 08h – 17h | **Maximum** |
| New York | 13h – 22h | Strong |

**Absolute peak** : **London + New York** overlap (13h–17h GMT)

## Market Events

### Classification

| Type | Origin | Example |
|------|--------|---------|
| **Endogenous** (*Endogenous*) | Inside the market | Liquidity crunch (*liquidity crunch*) |
| **Scheduled exogenous** (*Scheduled*) | External + known date | NFP, GDP, rate decisions |
| **Unscheduled exogenous** (*Unscheduled*) | External + surprise | Attacks, SNB decision 2011 |

### Key scheduled news

- **Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP)** : 1st Friday of the month · 8:30 EST (14:30 CH) · US employment
- **GDP** (*GDP*) : quarterly · economic growth
- **Rate decisions** : Fed, ECB, SNB

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — The deviation from expectations, not the absolute figure"}
What moves the market = **surprise** = published figure − expected consensus.
A good figure *below expectations* can make the market **fall**.
:::

---

## Summary — What markets are NOT

::: {.callout-note title="Markets ≠ random walk"}
Markets exhibit : volatility clustering · fat tails · seasonality · autocorrelation · scaling laws.

Causes : human interactions · herding behaviour · institutional constraints · algorithmic trading.
:::
